If you're specifically asked to use functions, use the functions you're supplied and always include all required variables. Don't use those functions unless you were asked to do so. You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected

I want a rectangular box that is 220mm wide, 300mm long and 160mm high. Let it be on the upside open and have walls with 8mm thickness and a 12mm thick bottom. | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Step-by-step plan (description only ‑ no execution yet)

1. Decide on a common base-point.  
   • Put the outside box so its lower-left-rear corner sits at the global origin (0, 0, 0).  
   • Positive X will represent the 220 mm width, positive Y the 300 mm length, positive Z the 160 mm height.

2. Build the outside “solid” volume.  
   • Call functions.block once with:  
     – x_size = 220, y_size = 300, z_size = 160  
     – x = 0, y = 0, z = 0 (base at origin)  
     – subtraction = False (it is the first, additive volume)

3. Carve out the inner cavity to leave 8 mm walls and a 12 mm bottom.  
   • Inner cavity starts after the wall thickness:  
     – In X: begin at 8 mm from the outside wall → x = 8, width = 220 − 2·8 = 204 mm  
     – In Y: begin at 8 mm → y = 8, length = 300 − 2·8 = 284 mm  
   • In Z: the bottom is 12 mm thick, so the cavity starts at z = 12 mm and rises all the way to the top:  
     – z = 12, height = 160 − 12 = 148 mm  
   • This block must be marked subtraction = True so it removes material.

4. Supply both blocks at once by passing arrays to a single functions.block call:  
   – x_size      = [220, 204]  
   – y_size      = [300, 284]  
   – z_size      = [160, 148]  
   – x           = [0, 8]  
   – y           = [0, 8]  
   – z           = [0, 12]  
   – subtraction = [False, True]

The result will be an open-top box 220 × 300 × 160 mm, walls 8 mm thick, and a 12 mm bottom.
